encounters.cc: Newborn with weakness of the right upper extremity noted immediately after birth

lines: Newborn with weakness of the right upper extremity noted immediately after birth
He was delivered via vaginal birth at 41 weeks gestation.
Labor was prolonged and complicated by shoulder dystocia, requiring the use of traction maneuvers to complete the delivery.
Since birth, the infant has not moved his right arm, though his left side is active and spontaneous.

The mother reports that the infant cries when the right arm is touched or moved.

encounters.cc: Follow-up for right arm weakness and lack of movement noted since birth

lines: Follow-up for right arm weakness and lack of movement noted since birth
The patient is a one-month-old macrosomic infant of a diabetic mother complicated by shoulder dystocia who returns for follow-up of right upper extremity weakness.
He carries a history of neonatal clavicular fracture, hypocalcemia, and transient hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
The mother reports that the infant was born at 41 weeks via vaginal delivery, and his birth weight was 4.5 kg.
She mentions that the delivery was difficult, and the obstetrician had to exert significant effort to deliver the infant's shoulders.
Since birth, she has noticed that the infant does not move his right arm and keeps it flexed and internally rotated.
The infant is feeding well and has no other health issues.

lines: Firm mass on the right side of his neck noticed a few days ago with head tilt

The patient is a 2-month-old male with a history of infant of diabetic mother, macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, and neonatal clavicular fracture, who returns to clinic following recent evaluation for right upper extremity neuromuscular impairment.
He is brought by his parents due to a firm mass on the right side of his neck that they first noticed a few days ago.
The parents deny any recent fever, fussiness, feeding difficulties, or signs of infection.
They state that the baby tends to keep his head turned slightly to the left, and they have noticed some asymmetry in how he holds his head when awake.
